Williams will transmit to staff for distribution: the GAU letter on Graduate Village housing; the letter about the spring final exam calendar with options and suggestions to solicit feedback from all faculty.

Call to Order - Pres.

VP Preisser and Senators Van Wyk, Meenach, Trimm and Daniels were present. 2.
Minutes for approval - i.
Minutes of the 03/06/26 FSEC meeting - The minutes were approved as edited. 3.
Priority Items (30 minutes) 3.1 Senate Meeting Recap - March 12 FS meeting (agenda) - FSEC members were pleased to have gotten through the agenda with only a couple of items tabled to the April meeting.
The amount of debate on specific agenda items is always difficult to predict and FSEC members agreed it is generally preferable to allot the luxury of time for discussion of important matters to the degree possible, and senators appreciate the happy surprise of wrapping up early if less time is needed.
The only real open question from the meeting is the question about scheduling a make-up day of instruction close to exams to cover the recent blizzard disruption.
Voting at the April 16 meeting on a suitable solution is an option, but that timeline leaves very little room getting the word out and making accommodations.

Another option would be for the senate to schedule a special online meeting to discuss the options and vote electronically (with a ratification of the proposed change on April 16) so that a decision can be shared earlier than 4/16 and planning can begin. 3.2 Advance Planning - April 16 FS meeting - The agenda is expected to include, among other things: an annual report from the Honors Program and possibly related University Manual amendments addressing the restructuring of the program as previously discussed; an annual report from the BAC as well as a presentation of the committee’s survey project and results; legislation related to the Ombuds; the JCODL bill for action.
The student senate has shown an interest in introducing legislation related to establishment of a syllabus bank but it is not known if a draft will actually be ready in time for review.
Such a bill would need to be carefully crafted if it is to gain support from faculty.
The student senate has stressed the need by noting that syllabi can be an important resource for students in determining the costs associated with courses. 3.3 Legislation Updates i.
FSEC Bill #09 (JCODL) - discussed as part of Item 3.2 above. 1

ii.
Honors update to UM 8.60.10 - 8.65.12 revisions/related HPR 000 course - The Honors program has submitted a draft that the FS officers will continue to refine.
It may be ready for introduction at the 4/16 meeting but will still require review and approval by TAAC and CBUM. iii.
UCAS/Fannon Institute - Amending Chapters 3, 5, and 8 of the UM.
The name change legislation was accepted at the 3/12 meeting, but the detailed structural and procedural changes will not be ready before the end of this academic year.
VP Preisser will need to make this a priority during his Presidential term. iv.
SCLC Ombuds Bill - Pres.
Williams has created a master document in hopes of producing a draft for vote at the April 16 FS meeting. v.
Student Senate Legislation (Syllabus Bank) - Discussed as part of Item 3.2 above. 4.
Continued Items 4.1 Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - There was a new inquiry related to the FSEC initiative to create an internal-facing survey design assistance team and whether or not the SSIREP was involved.
The SSIREP director was consulted and is in favor of the idea and agrees that the new initiative should stand alone.

There was also a new inquiry related to relocation of the INP from the Graduate School to CHS without consultation with affected faculty. i.
Follow-ups from past concerns a.
INP relocation from Graduate School to CHS - There was a flurry of inquiry when this transition was first approved, and CHS faculty have recently reached out again to note that, even if the change followed a procedurally acceptable path, it seems contrary to the spirit of collegiality that faculty are accustomed to experiencing for such a significant move to be proposed without any communication with affected parties.
FSEC members emphasized that it is important to advocate for faculty and shine a light on any concerning practices that negatively affect them.
Pres.
Williams will offer the senate’s public platform for CHS representatives to present the troubling recent events, highlight their related concerns, and remind fellow faculty members to be alert to any such proposals in their own colleges and programs. 4.2 Selecting Grubman and Wenisch Award winners - Winners were selected and staff will order awards.
Pres.
Williams and Sen.
Trimm volunteered to write the award letters. 5.

Updates/Ongoing Items 5.1 Updates (meetings with administrators, other committee meetings) - FS Pres.
Williams attended the most recent of the PSC and noted the presentations were focused on the effort to launch a medical school, and the efforts of the Marketing and Communications division to target audiences along the eastern seaboard to grow enrollment in online programs.
FSEC members noted, however, that there is always pressure on faculty to market their own programs and courses and it is an opaque process to determine how those faculty efforts intersect with the work of the VP CM’s team.
Also at the PSC meeting, Vice Provost Adams provided an update on the data collection efforts underway as part of the NECHE reaccreditation effort.
Finally, there was a brief presentation on the work of the Bias Reporting Team and the assistance they can provide to faculty in terms of routing concerns and complaints.
It was suggested that the senate consider intersections with the University Ombuds as amendments to that UM language move forward.
It was also suggested that the senate consider inviting a bias reporting presentation to the full senate at a future meeting. i.
CASC work on program description standardizations - See 6iii below. 2

ii.
Appeal from GAU re. closure of Graduate Village - A GAU representative made a presentation at the 3/12 FS meeting highlighting the timeline of the demolition and new construction project and the number of students displaced.
As a follow-up, the Faculty Senate President will be sharing a letter with all faculty addressing the issue and indicating ways that faculty might support affected students. iii.
Nominees to serve on SAC - A COEng representative has been recruited for confirmation at the 4/16 FS meeting. 6.
Report of the Coordinator i.
FSEC Recruitment - There are three seats opening and there are currently three senators interested in running.
The Nominating Committee will continue to reach out to suggested individuals and they have been reminded that senator elections in the colleges are coming up soon and newly elected senators are eligible for nomination.
It was noted there may be confusion about course releases associated with FSEC service.
Only the Pres. and VP are eligible for release and this messaging to senators needs to be clarified. ii.
